note: The ONLY place two differently-spelled names may become one person. tools/compile_gazetteer.py keys the gazetteer on the whole normalized name, so nothing coalesces by accident; anything that should coalesce is declared here, with the judgement written out. Three rules the compiler enforces: a merge needs a `merge_rule`; the rule must name BOTH spellings verbatim, so it can be read back without the code; and same surname with different initials NEVER merges, rule or no rule — the 1835 letter lists are full of families and an initial is often the only thing separating two of them.

merges.merge_rule: The 1 January 1834 Chicago letter list is printed three times, and its THIRD printing — chicago_democrat_1834_02_04 c016, the ruled-dialect impression that sets one name per line — reads at full length the name the 1834-01-28 impression cut to 'William Cr[…]': it is William Criss, standing between James Childress and Benj. Chapman in the first alphabetical column of both impressions. Exactly one person in the whole gazetteer carries that forename with a surname beginning 'Cri' — William Crisey, from the Chicago list of the following return, chicago_democrat_1834_03_04 c026 — and a letter remaining uncalled for across two consecutive returns of the same post office is what these lists are for. The two impressions disagree on the surname's tail, 'Criss' against 'Crisey'; the page images would settle which the printer set, and they do not bear on whether it is one man. T-0323.

The third printing of the 1 January 1834 Chicago letter list — chicago_democrat_1834_02_04 c016, one name per line — carries ONE name at this position: 'Orinda Gary', between Jacob Fake and William [Good]ing 2. The 1834-01-28 impression's extraction produced two adjacent entries across that one printed name, 'Orinds Guryl' and 'ds Gay”', minted as [uncertain: Orinda Guryl] and [?] Gay. The second is the tail of the first and not a second person, so the bare surname [?] Gay is closed by joining it to the entry that kept the forename rather than by supplying an initial it never had. T-0323.
